newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt softens, awaiting U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt softens, awaiting U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Swedish debt yields rose slightly in the early session on Friday, driven by weaker European markets. The crown firmed against a softer mark but lost ground against the dollar.
Early in the morning the dollar was quoted at eight crowns, although not necessarily traded at this level, and dealers said this psycological level could well be tested again.
"If the dollar breaks through the 1.8470 level against the mark, the crown may soften to trade above eight crowns to the dollar and firm below 4.3250 to the mark," one dealer said.

The market was holding its breath ahead of U.S. unemployment figures due at 1230 GMT. The data was expected to confirm non-inflationary U.S. economy. Non-farm payrolls expected at 193,000 from 217,000 in June.
Unemployment was expected to tick down to 4.9 percent from five percent.

The ten-year bond yield rose two basis points to 6.40 percent and the six-month T-bill rates climbed one basis point to 4.29 percent. The crown firmed to 4.3310 against the mark from 4.3335 and dropped to 7.9893 against the dollar from 7.9684. -- Barbara Taltavull, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1019
